title: Implement idempotency keys for the checkout endpoint
business_context: PayLane's checkout endpoint (POST /checkout) charges customers through a payment provider whose network occasionally times out mid-request. Mobile clients retry timeouts automatically, so a slow provider response currently means the customer gets charged twice while support eats the tickets. The endpoint and its request/response contract are frozen; the mobile team has agreed to send an Idempotency-Key header once this feature ships.
user_request: Implement idempotency keys for POST /checkout so provider timeouts can be retried safely. The mobile team will send an Idempotency-Key header. Design it so a retried request can never double-charge, and make sure a failure can always be retried. Existing behaviour (no header) must not change.

task.feature_spec: POST /checkout accepts an optional Idempotency-Key header. Scope: keys are per customer (the order's customer_id). Behaviour: (1) A charge request carrying a key, whose provider call succeeds, stores the response body under (key, customer). (2) A retry with the same (key, customer) returns the stored response body byte-for-byte with HTTP 200 and must NOT charge again nor write a second charge row. (3) A request with no key behaves exactly as today. (4) A provider failure (non-2xx or missing reference) is NOT stored: a retry with the same key performs a fresh charge. (5) The same key used by a different customer is a different operation (charges normally). You may add tables/migrations. The charge rows must record customer_id and the provider reference.

non_obvious_invariant: Replay must be keyed by (Idempotency-Key, customer) — a global key namespace leaks one customer's charge result to another; only SUCCESSFUL provider outcomes may be stored, otherwise a failed first attempt becomes a permanent 500 replay; and a replay must not write a second charge row.
expected_diagnosis: Not applicable (build task): the agent must design storage for (key, customer, response), branch on the header, gate the provider call behind the replay check, and store only successful outcomes — distinguishing transport success from provider success.
safe_fix_constraints: POST /checkout keeps its request/response contract for header-less requests (existing JSON shape byte-identical).
You may add tables/migrations and models; do not add composer dependencies.
The visible suite must stay green before and after your change.
failure_explanation: Without idempotency keys every mobile retry after a provider timeout double-charges the customer. A global key namespace replays customer A's charge response to customer B (cross-customer data leak); storing failed outcomes turns a transient provider outage into a permanent 500 for that key.
